Laborious

/luh-BOR-ee-uhs/ - the stress falls on BOR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Laborious means requiring long, slow, careful toil.

Untangling and re-knotting the trawler's half-mile net after every voyage was laborious work that cost the crew a full day in port.

Worked Example

Before spreadsheets, the co-op's bookkeeper closed each month the laborious way: seven ledgers reconciled line by line, three evenings of patient checking, and a single slipped digit could send her back to the top of the column.

Laborious emphasizes the slow, grinding quality of work - toil measured in patient hours rather than bursts of strength. A laborious task is not necessarily heavy; it is long, careful, and wearying.

How Laborious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

toilsome

toilsome: full of hard, wearying toil

plodding

plodding: slow and heavy-footed, without spark

Antonyms

quick

quick: done in little time

light

light: asking little effort

How Strong Is It? — time-consuming → laborious → backbreaking

time-consuming vs. laborious

time-consuming vs. laborious: Time-consuming only says a task eats hours; laborious adds toil - the hours are full of slow, careful effort.

backbreaking vs. laborious

backbreaking vs. laborious: Backbreaking outdoes laborious on the body: laborious work wears you down over patient hours, while backbreaking work grinds muscle and spine directly.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — labor

Root — labor: work, toil

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Labor (work, toil) + -ious (full of) = full of work. The root is the everyday English word labor itself, carried straight from Latin, and it still works hard across the language - most visibly in laboratory, originally 'a place for work.'

Use the root in a new word: laboratory

Use the root in a new word: laboratory: The chemistry laboratory is literally a 'work-place' - a room built for careful labor.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Laborious points at the toil inside a task: long, slow, effortful. Its unit-mates divide the territory - arduous stresses that the whole undertaking is difficult and tiring, while strenuous says the demand falls on the body's strength and stamina. A tax form can be laborious without being strenuous; a sprint is strenuous without being laborious.
